verdict_reason: The species check is wired correctly for drafts, but its gating is split between the controller flag and refusal.js under a mispredicting name, the refusal is not logged, and existing comments break the house rules.

todos.issue: checksSpeciesAgainstMdm (lines 156-159) is true for a refused amend, but speciesCardErrors (refusal.js:27) returns {} for any status but DRAFT, so no check runs; the draft-only rule lives in refusal.js and the refused-only rule here, two homes deciding when species are checked. The name also uses a fourth word for one concept (AgainstMdm here, linesWithUnlistedSpecies in species-check.js, speciesNoLongerOffered in copy, SPECIES_MDM_DOES_NOT_LIST in the test), and this module calls reference-data, not MDM.
todos.fix: Must: one place decides when a draft's species are checked, and the flag (if kept) is named for what it is true for in every state, using the same concept word as speciesCardErrors and linesWithUnlistedSpecies. One way: drop the flag and pass the refused state to speciesCardErrors (like documentScanCardErrors' includePending), letting it own both the draft and the refused rule.

todos.issue: A draft refused because reference-data no longer lists a stored species (speciesErrors, lines 156-159 and isReviewRefused) logs nothing, here or in refusal.js / species-check.js. Another service refusing an answer this one accepted is a decision support must see: during an incident they cannot tell which journey, code or Latin name was refused, or that MDM data changed under saved drafts.
todos.fix: Must: each refusal for an unlisted species logs once at warn with the journey id and every refused code and Latin name. One way: log in speciesCardErrors when unlisted is non-empty, using request.logger passed in or the module logger, with { journeyId, unlisted }.

todos.issue: Comments break the house rules: the JSDoc block on lines 39-51 is a doc comment on a non-exported constant, describes reviewErrorSummary and the page's focus behaviour rather than the line below it, and holds rationale; lines 169-172 explain why the maps are spread in this order (rationale), now over four maps including the new speciesErrors.
todos.fix: Must: no comment in the file holds rationale or describes code other than the lines directly below it, and no doc comment sits on an internal helper. One way: move the precedence and party-key rationale to the live-animals docs/ or the behaviour spec, name the precedence in code (e.g. a helper such as incompleteOverridesInvalid), and delete both comments.
